blocks.text: PROSPERIDAD, Agusan del Sur — Weeks after severe dry spells and erratic weather prompted a provincial state of calamity, farmers and fisherfolk across Agusan del Sur are shifting from emergency response to active defense, applying new weather-informed techniques to safeguard their livelihoods. After P3.5 billion in agricultural losses from the prolonged El Niño dry spell, communities in Bayugan City and Talacogon are using lessons from an intensive provincial training caravan organized by the Provincial Agriculture and Veterinary Office (PAVO). Instead of relying on rigid, traditional planting schedules, trained farmers and fisherfolk are now actively tracking meteorological bulletins and recalibrating field routines […]...
